issues.explanation: At the 0.5 cut-off, 104 of the 141 flagged test advertisers churned, not 134. Stating 134 contradicts facts.json, disagrees with the segment's own confusion-matrix visual (tp = 104), and fails to add up with the 37 false alarms (134 + 37 = 171, not 141).
issues.evidence: facts.json -> logreg.test: flagged = 141, tp = 104, fp = 37 (also thresholds[7] at threshold = 0.5: tp = 104).
issues.fix: Change 'Of those, 134 really churned.' to 'Of those, 104 really churned.'

issues.quote: Recall, remember, is the share of your flags that turn out to be right, so a model with high recall rarely wastes a call.
issues.explanation: This sentence defines precision rather than recall and directly contradicts both standard ML definitions and earlier narration in segments 4 and 5. The share of flags that turn out to be right is precision; recall is the share of actual churners that were flagged. A model with high recall can still waste many calls on false alarms (for example, flagging everyone gives 100% recall).
issues.evidence: Recall = TP / (TP + FN) (share of actual positives caught), whereas precision = TP / (TP + FP) (share of flags that are truly positive); see also facts.json -> uncertainty.recall_at_half_95 = [0.165, 0.235].
issues.fix: Remove this sentence or replace it with the bootstrap uncertainty interval for recall from facts.json: 'And recall could land anywhere from about 17 to 24 percent.'

issues.explanation: The recall formula visual transposes the digits of the test-set churner total, dividing 104 by 257 instead of 527. Dividing 104 by 257 gives 40.5%, contradicting the 19.7% result on the next line, the narration ('104 out of 527'), and facts.json.
issues.evidence: facts.json -> data.churners_test = 527; logreg.test: tp = 104, fn = 423 (104 + 423 = 527), recall = 0.197 (104 / 527 = 0.1973).

issues.quote: and its recall about 41, far above
issues.explanation: The hand rule 'spend_trend < 0.7' catches 246 of the 527 test churners, giving a recall of 46.7% (about 47 percent), not about 41 percent. Stating 41 contradicts facts.json as well as the segment's own visual table ('46.7%') and later narration ('nearly half the churners').
issues.fix: Change 'and its recall about 41, far above.' to 'and its recall about 47 percent, far above.'

verdict: Fail: four high-severity errors must be fixed before publication—three numeric mismatches against facts.json (134 vs 104 true positives in seg3 narration, 257 vs 527 churners in seg5 visual, and 41% vs 46.7% rule recall in seg6 narration) and a false conceptual statement at the end of seg5 narration that defines recall as precision.
